note: Pieces of Natural Earth's modern countries that changed hands inside the period, split out so a polity can be assembled from them. A part is taken out of its source and the source keeps the remainder, so nothing is ever in two parts at once. `within` takes whole polygons falling inside [west, south, east, north]; `clip` cuts against a drawn shape. Carves are applied in the order written here, each cutting from whatever its source has left — so a later carve may be drawn generously where it abuts ground an earlier one already took. Referenced by id from the files in data/polities/.

french-guiana.name: French Guiana
french-guiana.why: Natural Earth stores French Guiana with France. Splitting the separate mainland polygon lets the colonial and modern territory be represented without drawing metropolitan France.

crimea.name: Crimea
crimea.why: Natural Earth draws Crimea as part of Russia. Splitting it out lets it sit under Ukraine before 2014 and Russia after.

alaska.name: Alaska
alaska.why: Russian America until 1867. The box clears the contiguous states, whose northernmost point is 49.4N, and Hawaii, which lies far to the south.

aleutians-west.name: Western Aleutians
aleutians-west.why: Six islands of the Aleutian chain that Natural Earth draws past the antimeridian, so they miss the Alaska box entirely. Held by whoever holds `alaska`.

texas.name: Texas
texas.why: Spanish, then Mexican, then an independent republic, then annexed in 1845. Carved first, so the Louisiana Purchase and the Mexican Cession can be drawn generously where they meet it. Drawn as the modern state plus the Oklahoma panhandle, which the Republic held and gave up in 1850; the Republic's wider claim north into Colorado and Wyoming was never controlled and is not drawn. The southern and western edges run out into Mexico and the Gulf, because the real limit there is the source's own coastline and river border.

louisiana-purchase.name: Louisiana Purchase
louisiana-purchase.why: Bought from France in 1803. The eastern edge is the Mississippi, the western the Continental Divide, and the southern the Adams-Onis line of 1819 — up the 100th meridian from the Red River to the Arkansas, then up the Arkansas to its source. The northern edge runs above the 49th parallel because the real limit there is the source's own border with Canada. It reaches past the Mississippi at the bottom to take the Isle of Orleans, which was the point of the purchase, and swings east of the delta's outer passes so the whole delta stays with the river rather than falling to `florida`. The Florida Parishes north of it are `florida-parishes`.

florida.name: Florida
florida.why: Spanish Florida as the Adams-Onis treaty settled it in 1819: the peninsula, the panhandle, and the Gulf coast strip of Alabama, Mississippi and the Florida Parishes of Louisiana that made up West Florida. The western edge may be drawn out past the Mississippi because the Louisiana Purchase has already taken everything on that side.

mobile-district.name: Mobile district
mobile-district.why: The Gulf coast from the Pearl to the Perdido: Biloxi from 1699 and Mobile from 1702, French until 1763 and then the western half of British West Florida. Spain held Pensacola, east of the Perdido, throughout, so the cut stops there. Carved out of `florida` because Spain never held this coast in the century the French were on it.

florida-parishes.name: Florida Parishes
florida-parishes.why: The east bank between the Mississippi and the Pearl, north of the lakes that make the Isle of Orleans an island. French from the concessions of the 1720s, British West Florida in 1763, Spanish only from 1783 — so it cannot sit inside `florida` for the whole period. The box takes everything `florida` still has in that span of the river; the French shape drawn over it stops at the lakes.

oregon-country.name: Oregon Country
oregon-country.why: Held jointly with Britain from 1818 until the treaty of 1846 split it at the 49th parallel. Only the southern edge has to be exact — 42N, still the California-Oregon line. The eastern edge is a meridian well past the Continental Divide, because the Louisiana Purchase has already taken everything east of it.

gadsden-purchase.name: Gadsden Purchase
gadsden-purchase.why: Bought from Mexico in 1854, for a southern railroad route. Bounded north by the border Guadalupe Hidalgo drew in 1848 — west along 31.8N to the 108th meridian, north to the Gila, then down the Gila to the Colorado — and south by the modern border, which is the source's own edge.

mexican-cession.name: Mexican Cession
mexican-cession.why: Taken from Mexico in 1848: California, Nevada, Utah, and the parts of Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado and Wyoming that Texas, the Louisiana Purchase, Oregon and the Gadsden Purchase have not already claimed. Drawn as a plain box for exactly that reason — it is whatever is left in the southwest.

confederacy-east.name: The Confederacy east of the Mississippi
confederacy-east.why: Virginia, the Carolinas, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee. Carved from what is left of the original United States once Florida has been taken, so only the northern frontier has to be drawn: the Potomac to the Fairfax Stone, the Mason-Dixon line, the Ohio, the Big Sandy, and then the Kentucky-Tennessee line — Kentucky and Maryland stayed in the Union, so the border runs well south of the Ohio in the west. The southern and eastern edges run out into the Gulf and the Atlantic.

west-virginia.name: West Virginia
west-virginia.why: The western counties refused to leave the Union and were admitted as a state of their own in 1863, so they cannot stay inside Virginia. Only the boundary with Virginia is drawn — the rest is the frontier `confederacy-east` has already established, which is why this clip may run north into Pennsylvania. The line is far more ragged on the ground than at this tolerance.

confederacy-west.name: The Confederacy west of the Mississippi
confederacy-west.why: Louisiana and Arkansas, the two Purchase states that seceded. Bounded north by the Arkansas-Missouri line at 36.5N, with the notch that keeps the Missouri bootheel in the Union, and west by the Arkansas line at 94.62W. Everything else is the Purchase's own edge.

newfoundland.name: Newfoundland
newfoundland.why: A separate British colony, then a dominion of its own, until it joined Canada in 1949.

labrador.name: Labrador
labrador.why: Attached to Newfoundland in 1809 and joined Canada with it in 1949, so it cannot sit inside Quebec. The boundary is the height of land the Privy Council settled in 1927, drawn to the tolerance this map renders at.

arctic-archipelago.name: Arctic Archipelago
arctic-archipelago.why: Britain kept the northern islands when it transferred Rupert's Land in 1870 and handed them over separately in 1880. The box takes only whole islands north of 60N; the mainland polygon reaches down to 41.7N and so is left alone.

prince-edward-island.name: Prince Edward Island
prince-edward-island.why: Stayed out of Confederation until 1873. The box stops short of Cape Breton, which reaches east to 59.8W.

british-columbia.name: British Columbia
british-columbia.why: A separate colony on the Pacific until it joined Canada in 1871. Bounded east by the 120th meridian down to 53.8N and then the Continental Divide, north by 60N with the Yukon above it, and west by open ocean — the Alaska panhandle belongs to another country and so is not in this source.

oregon-country-north.name: Oregon Country, north of the Columbia
oregon-country-north.why: The Oregon Country ran from 42N to 54 degrees 40 minutes — the southern limit of Russian America — so half of it is ground that is British Columbia today. Splitting it out is what lets the whole of it be contested between Britain and the United States before 1846, instead of the 49th parallel appearing on the map twenty-eight years before the treaty drew it. Only the northern edge is drawn; east and west are already British Columbia's own limits.

province-of-canada.name: Canada East and West, New Brunswick and Nova Scotia
province-of-canada.why: The four provinces that federated in 1867, leaving Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory as the remainder of CAN. Only the northern edge is drawn: Ontario stopped at the Albany River and Quebec at the Eastmain, and everything above was the Hudson's Bay Company's. The southern and eastern edges run out into the United States and the Atlantic, where the real limit is the source's own coastline.

french-antilles.name: French Antilles
french-antilles.why: Martinique, Guadeloupe and its dependencies, which Natural Earth draws as part of France rather than as codes of their own.

dutch-caribbean.name: Dutch Caribbean
dutch-caribbean.why: Bonaire, Saba and Sint Eustatius, which Natural Earth draws as part of the Netherlands. Aruba, Curacao and Sint Maarten have codes of their own.
